findings.plain_title: Nothing checks that the build Vercel runs still runs the auth-token leak check
findings.engine_title: testing gap: nothing pins that web/package.json's build still ends with the token check after next build
findings.engine_why_it_matters: The new tests in tooling/assert-no-auth-token.test.mjs copy the build's invocation by hand and are named 'run as the build runs it', but nothing reads the build line. Deleting the step, moving it before next build, or changing its form keeps every test and CI job green while production loses the guard between SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN and browser-served files; CI builds run with no token, so they never exercise it for real.
findings.engine_suggested_fix: One assertion in tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs (which already reads web/package.json scripts at line 229), for example assert.match(packageJson('web/package.json').scripts.build, /next build && .*&& node scripts\/assert-no-auth-token\.mjs$/).
findings.engine_validator: not sent to the engine's validator (testing gaps are not); this loop's verifier confirmed it with mutations
findings.severity_meaning: P3 = low impact, narrow scope; the owner's discretion
findings.confidence_meaning: no score: the engine lists testing gaps without one. This loop's verifier proved the gap with a mutation check (see 'spike').
findings.verified: pass — no test reads web/package.json's build line or web/vercel.json's buildCommand. With the step deleted, moved before next build, or given an absolute path, all 108 tooling tests stayed green.
findings.scenario: Months from now you edit web's build line: you add a step or reorder it, and the token check falls off, or ends up before `next build`. Every test and CI job stays green, because CI builds run without a token, so the check passes there whether it runs or not. The next production build on Vercel runs with the real SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, and nothing checks that the token stayed out of the files sent to browsers.
findings.whats_wrong: Lap 1's F-1 tests run the token check 'the way the build runs it', but they copy that command by hand (`node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs`, from web/). Nothing reads the real build line in web/package.json, or the buildCommand in web/vercel.json that Vercel actually runs.

findings.proposed_fix: Add one test to tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs, next to the test that already reads web/package.json scripts: vercel.json must still run `pnpm run build`, and web's build must run `node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs` as a step after `next build`.
findings.why_it_works: It reads the two lines Vercel actually runs, so each of the three edits in the scenario fails exactly this one test (proven by mutation).
findings.trade_off: Strict on purpose: a deliberate change to either build line — even `./scripts/…` or `pnpm build` in vercel.json — must update this test, and its comment says so. It raises no false alarm for dropping the unrelated CSS step or for adding a later step. It also catches vercel.json skipping the build script, and `|| true` added to the line.

spike.result: workflow-guards 13/13 → 14/14; all tooling tests 108/108 → 109/109; assert-no-auth-token unchanged at 10/10; prettier, cspell and editorconfig pass (tooling/ has no ESLint config). Mutations of web/package.json — step deleted, moved before next build, absolute path — each fail only the new test, with the message: web's build must run "node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs" after next build.

findings.recommendation: Apply: it closes the gap lap 1's F-1 was about, five of the eight reviewers raised it, and it costs one test. Flip to Skip if you plan to rework the build line soon.
findings.missing_context: The reviewers' candidate regex read only web/package.json; the spike also reads web/vercel.json, because Vercel runs `rm -rf .next/cache && pnpm run build` from web/. That regex would also raise false alarms if the CSS step were dropped or a later step added.
findings.recorded_decisions: Lap 1 F-1 (the token check's tests, applied; the build starts the script by a relative path, so the symlink limit is safe). This test turns that premise from assumed into checked. Lap 1's FYI about the entry check and symlinks stays as it is.
